summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored Grenada documents: Ministry of Finance CBI statistics sheets (Mar 2014-Dec 2015 monthly, 2016 by half-year, Jan-Sep 2017), IMA quarterly statistics (Q4 2024, Q4 2025, Q1 2026) and processing report, IMF Article IV reports 2016, 2019, 2023, 2024 and 2025, budget statements 2024-2026, an IMA circular, two web pages and two EU documents. Added every cell of the statistics sheets (by month, route and money line, including geographic shares of applications), the full IMF table lines for CBI revenue, CBI inflows and bondholder payments for all years, price terms from IMA Circular No. 2 and IMF Box 1, and dated rule changes. 19 documents complete, 1 partial (EU visa report whose twin intl-ec-com-2025-792 holds its numbers).

observations.location: p. 1, 'Geographic Distribution of Applications Year-to-Date' legend, NIGERIA
observations.notes: 'Geographic Distribution of Applications Year-to-Date' (pie chart with a printed legend of percentages). The sheet does not say whether the shares are by nationality or by country of residence, nor whether the base is applications received or accepted (recorded with breakdown country=). Percentages as printed (whole numbers). The 19 printed shares add up to 101 (rounding). 'Other' is defined on the sheet: '"Other" includes applications received from countries that are not listed. Each unlisted country represents 1% or less of total applications accepted by the Agency', followed by a list of about 40 countries without percentages.

events.title: IMA Circular No. 2: new prices from 1 July 2024 and cut-off for old prices
events.description: IMA told agents and developers that the OECS Memorandum of Agreement pricing (NTF US$235,000; approved project US$270,000 plus US$50,000 government contribution) takes effect on 1 July 2024; only complete applications lodged with the Grenada Co-operative Bank by 30 June 2024 are accepted at the old prices, with funds cleared by 31 July 2024. Agents' commission capped at US$35,000 (NTF) and US$40,000 (approved project). Superseded on 3 July by Circular No. 3, which moved the deadline to 12 July 2024.
events.quote: a new pricing structure for the Investment Migration Agency Grenada (IMA) will be implemented effective July 1, 2024

events.title: EU concludes the short-stay visa waiver agreement with Grenada
events.description: Council Decision (EU) 2016/270 approves, on behalf of the EU, the agreement on the short-stay visa waiver for Grenadian citizens (applied provisionally since 28 May 2015; European Parliament consent 15 December 2015). The date of entry into force was to be published separately.
events.location: Article 1; footnote (1) to the preamble; signature
events.quote: The Agreement between the European Union and Grenada on the short-stay visa waiver is hereby approved on behalf of the Union.

events.title: National Transformation Fund Regulations put in place
events.description: Regulations for the National Transformation Fund (the fund receiving CBI donations) were approved in August 2015 (a structural benchmark due 28 February 2015). They require forty percent of monthly NTF inflows to be saved for general budget financing (contingencies, natural disasters, debt reduction), NTF spending to be limited to non-recurrent productive infrastructure, and a Board of Directors for the NTF (planned by end-2016).
events.location: PDF p. 67, MEFP para 10; PDF p. 77, structural benchmark 5
events.quote: Adhere to the regulations for the NTF, put in place in August 2015.

events.title: First allocations to the savings (natural disaster) fund from NTF savings
events.description: IMF reports that resources were allocated in August 2018 to the savings fund being set up from a portion of the National Transformation Fund's savings (a natural disaster fund); regulations for its use were under review.
events.location: PDF p. 43, Annex (implementation of past recommendations)
events.quote: Resource allocations to the savings fund were made in August 2018 and the regulations for its usage are under review.

events.title: CBI donations recorded as non-tax revenue instead of grants from 2023
events.description: Grenada's fiscal accounts record the non-refundable contributions under the CBI programme as non-tax revenue starting in 2023; before 2023, contributions used to finance investment projects were recorded under grants. IMF says the change improves the programme's transparency and follows the view of its Committee on Balance of Payments Statistics.
events.location: PDF p. 14, footnote 8 and footnote to the fiscal projections text table
events.quote: the nonrefundable contribution to the CBI program is recorded as non-tax revenues, instead of grants, starting 2023.

events.title: Lower threshold for the CBI investment option (as described by IMF)
events.description: IMF attributes stronger 2022 CBI flows to private investment to 'a lower threshold for the investment program'; the report gives neither the old nor the new amount nor a date.
events.quote: stronger financial account from CBI flows to private investment

events.title: Part of NTF receipts to be set aside monthly for the new hospital (Project Polaris)
events.description: The 2025 Budget Statement announced that a small percentage of all National Transformation Fund receipts would be set aside monthly from June 2025, after the legal requirements were finalised, to support the transition to the new hospital (Project Polaris). The percentage is not stated.
events.location: PDF p. 17 (printed p. 16), Advancing Project Polaris
events.quote: a small percentage of all NTF receipts will be set aside monthly, commencing June 2025 after finalizing the legal requirements

events.title: 10% of NTF receipts set aside in a contingency fund at the ECCB
events.description: Since April 2023 the government has paid 10 percent of National Transformation Fund (CBI donation) receipts into a contingency fund at the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank for disaster response (EC$61.1 million by late 2025). The 2025 Budget Statement says the set-aside was reduced from the 40 percent required under the earlier rules, which it says were never applied.
events.quote: Since April of 2023, we have set aside 10 percent of receipts into the National Transformation Fund into a Contingency Fund at the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank

events.title: Enhanced Local Developer Policy advanced by the IMA
events.description: The 2026 Budget Statement says the Investment Migration Agency advanced an 'Enhanced Local Developer Policy' in 2025, opening the CBI approved-project route to Grenadian developers, and that the CBI legislation is to be repealed and replaced in 2026 ahead of the regional regulator ECCIRA.
events.quote: the Agency advanced the Enhanced Local Developer Policy, opening new pathways for Grenadian developers
